items.streamTitle: Human numerosity signals emerged before non-numeric visual features
items.streamSummary: Time-resolved MEG and fMRI analyses found rapid numerosity signals preceding some non-numeric image-feature coding, with representations evolving from broad quantity to tuned number responses. Neural representational evidence does not imply numeric framing changes real-world decisions.
items.attribution: Karami, Castaldi, Eger, Hebart and Piazza — Nature Communications (MEG/fMRI representational study; November 19, 2026)

items.streamTitle: NATO called for exercising information-sharing and prioritization under digital disruption
items.streamSummary: At a November 18 conference, NATO and industry leaders emphasized exercising prioritization, information-sharing, surge support and service continuity when civilian digital infrastructure is disrupted. These are readiness objectives, not measured exercise outcomes.
items.attribution: NATO — NATO Cyber Defence Conference account (official operational coordination statement; November 19, 2026; meeting November 18)

items.streamTitle: Deepfake detector adaptation showed statistical ties despite apparent AUC leadership
items.streamSummary: With equal adapter parameter budgets on CLIP ViT-L/14 and six external test datasets, attention Q/V adaptation had the highest observed mean AUC (0.9432), but bootstrap intervals included zero for family comparisons; inference speed rankings were not established.
items.attribution: Kim and Kang — Scientific Reports (cross-dataset face-forgery detection benchmark; November 19, 2026)

items.streamTitle: NATO released a strategy for interoperable, resilient next-generation communications
items.streamSummary: NATO publicly released its NGCN strategy summary covering 5G/6G, SATCOM, interoperability, vendor trust and cyber/hybrid resilience. A Finland–Sweden-led innovation range supports testing, but published capability or behavioral outcomes were not supplied.
items.attribution: NATO — Next Generation Communication Networks Strategy public summary (official technical strategy release; November 18, 2026)

items.streamTitle: Career exploration's prospective link to confidence weakened in a sensitivity test
items.streamSummary: In 1,080 Beijing students, social support, career confidence, exploration and adaptability were associated. A positive three-month exploration-to-self-efficacy link in 265 students disappeared when excluded outliers were retained, limiting directional claims.
items.attribution: Kang, Liu, Chen et al. — Scientific Reports (adolescent survey and two-wave panel; November 18, 2026)

items.streamTitle: Embodied AI social benchmarks exposed gaps between perception and interaction
items.streamSummary: ALIVE-World evaluated 12 VLM agents in embodied retail and group discussions, separating social perception, understanding, influence and task outcome. Gaze, adaptive interaction and multiparty coordination were weak; simulated counterparts are not validated human audiences.
items.attribution: Xu, Qin, Zhao, Xiong and Jia — ALIVE-World/ALIVE-Bench, ACM Multimedia 2026 / arXiv preprint (November 16)

items.streamTitle: Selective robustness tests separated harmless prompt changes from meaningful simulated decisions
items.streamSummary: A social-agent simulation methodology distinguishes robustness to meaning-preserving prompt paraphrases from sensitivity to actual decision-relevant context. Different enrichment styles produced model-specific results in a Prisoner's Dilemma-like task.
items.attribution: Greiche, Rabbany and Puelma Touzel — arXiv preprint (two-model social-agent context experiment; November 4, 2026)

items.streamTitle: Adolescents increasingly inferred latent motives to predict unfamiliar social choices
items.streamSummary: In 127 Dutch participants aged 10–20, prediction across varied economic games improved with age; computational models attributed part of that pattern to inferring motives such as risk aversion rather than memorizing prior actions. Model attribution is not a causal developmental test.
items.attribution: Vigil-Escalera, van Baar, Molleman, van Duijvenvoorde and Ma — iScience (economic-game and computational study; online October 27, 2026)

items.streamTitle: Randomized team assignments identified causes of professional social ties
items.streamSummary: Using repeated employee networks and random initial project-team assignments, a causal network-formation framework found indirect ties strongly increased later tie formation, while degree and local density effects were less robust. A single-firm setting limits transfer.
items.attribution: Kasy, Linos and Mobasseri — CESifo Working Paper 12778 (design-based network-formation causal inference; 2026)

items.streamTitle: Redesigned multi-agent decision support failed to outperform a single model after stricter testing
items.streamSummary: A November 18 retrospective SMARTriage study found initial 88.2% apparent accuracy was vulnerable to development reuse and documentation leakage; locked re-evaluation favored simpler single-agent baselines by AUC. No clinical field utility was established.
items.attribution: Tsafrir, Arama, Ben Haim and Saban — Scientific Reports (retrospective AI decision-support evaluation; November 18, 2026)

items.streamTitle: Multimodal moderation prototype combined video, audio and text threat detection
items.streamSummary: A November 18 Scientific Reports prototype combined vision, speech, audio and text models and reported 98.33% overall detection accuracy. Real-platform robustness, category-specific errors and changes in harm were not independently demonstrated.
items.attribution: Manikandan, Swarna and Nivetha — Scientific Reports (multimodal content-moderation prototype; November 18, 2026)

items.streamTitle: AI and teacher feedback produced similar overall training gains in a small randomized crossover
items.streamSummary: An eight-week study analyzed 36 pre-service teachers after 46 were recruited: instructional-design skill rose in both human–AI and teacher-guided settings, without a reliable overall difference. Attrition, one institution and short follow-up constrain transfer.
items.attribution: Wang, Zhang, Zheng, Jiang, Gao and Li — Frontiers in Psychology (crossover educational experiment; November 17, 2026)

items.streamTitle: Dyadic decision-making increased risk taking and changed neural feedback responses
items.streamSummary: A November 11 EEG study found more risk-taking during dyadic than solo sequential decisions, with differing FRN and P3b feedback responses; one framing interaction did not survive correction. Evidence is from a laboratory risk task.
items.attribution: Li, Gao and Li — Biological Psychology (dyadic behavioral/EEG experiment; November 11, 2026)

items.streamTitle: UK government updated guidance for communicating accurately through AI-generated search answers
items.streamSummary: Updated November 17, the UK Government Communications PRIME framework recommends auditing public information, structuring answers for AI search and monitoring errors. It specifies a workflow, not proven improvement in trust or audience outcomes.
items.attribution: UK Government Communications — Strengthening public trust in the age of AI-powered search (official guidance; published October 20, updated November 17, 2026)

items.streamTitle: Social learning responded to payoff alignment and group identity, not majority size alone
items.streamSummary: In incentivized Swiss and Kenyan experiments, the same majority cue was interpreted differently depending on demonstrators' payoff alignment and ingroup status. Cognitive load affected memory but not reliably social-information use; human strategies varied by site.
items.attribution: von Flüe, Vogt and Efferson — Journal of Experimental Psychology: General (cross-population incentivized experiments; online August 31, November issue)

items.streamTitle: IPTC clarified which publisher certificates validate signed media provenance
items.streamSummary: An IPTC technical annex updated November 16 defines machine-readable publisher certificate lists for C2PA and CAWG checks. It enables more precise provenance verification but does not certify factual truth or demonstrate audience effects.
items.attribution: International Press Telecommunications Council — Verified News Publisher Policy: Technical Annex (official technical standard; updated November 16, 2026)

items.streamTitle: Mouse experiments linked motor-memory decay to removal of learning-associated myelin
items.streamSummary: Mouse experiments showed microglial removal of motor-learning-associated myelin contributes to memory decay, with CD47 manipulation changing decay. Generalization to human knowledge or training retention is untested.
items.attribution: Hu, Luo, Zhou et al. — Nature Neuroscience (mouse causal neurobiology experiments; November 17, 2026)

items.streamTitle: Preschool children showed appearance-based peer preferences in controlled comparisons
items.streamSummary: In 139 children aged three to seven, controlled same-face image comparisons showed graded hypothetical peer preferences by visible dental condition. The result measures immediate appearance-based judgments, not actual friendships.
items.attribution: Benke, Zsido, Basler et al. — Scientific Reports (preschool choice experiment; November 17, 2026)

items.streamTitle: AI dependence predicted lower critical-thinking disposition across three teacher-training waves
items.streamSummary: A three-wave study of 461 Chinese pre-service teachers associated greater AI dependence with lower critical-thinking disposition; AI self-efficacy partially mediated and stress moderated one path. Observational associations are not causal effects.
items.attribution: Zhu, Yang, Long et al. — Scientific Reports (three-wave longitudinal survey; November 17, 2026)

items.streamTitle: LLM public-opinion estimates approximated aggregate surveys but distorted partisan distributions
items.streamSummary: Three studies benchmarked LLM estimates against Pew polling: some aggregate estimates approached survey distributions, but partisan bias, excessive homogeneity and inferior persona-aggregation threatened validity. LLM answers are not human survey observations.
items.attribution: Li, Wang, Xie et al. — Humanities and Social Sciences Communications (public-opinion benchmarking; November 17, 2026)

items.streamTitle: Open tract-level synthetic populations preserve demographic–health joint structure
items.streamSummary: SHAPE released open 2024 U.S. tract/county synthetic populations and validated health-related small-area estimates against CDC data. It is a reproducible population-data infrastructure, not a behavioral influence prediction model.
items.attribution: Von Hoene, Gupta, Von Hoene et al. — Scientific Data (SHAPE public dataset and GIS tools; November 17, 2026)

items.streamTitle: CSIS assessed PLA mission-command and joint-warfighting vulnerabilities behind modernization
items.streamSummary: A November 16 CSIS report argues that PLA modernization may mask vulnerabilities in command, joint operations, logistics, dynamic targeting and corruption. It is interview-informed operational assessment, not measured wartime performance.
items.attribution: Jones, Heginbotham and Byman — CSIS, Peace Disease: Is the PLA Battle Ready? (research report; November 16, 2026)

items.streamTitle: Video-detector research found periodic decoding signatures in many generated clips
items.streamSummary: A November 16 preprint detected periodic video-decoder traces across many generators and improved benchmark detector AUROC. The results concern synthetic-video classification, not verified operational detection or reduced influence.
items.attribution: Sun, Li, Mei and Shou — arXiv preprint, VAE Rhythm (generated-video forensics benchmark; November 16, 2026)

items.streamTitle: Continuous-time causal-graph theory characterized what can be learned under latent confounding
items.streamSummary: W-separation yields formal, testable equivalence classes for continuous-time causal graphs with hidden common causes. It advances identification theory but supplies no validated human intervention forecasts.
items.attribution: Kempf, Kilbertus and Manten — arXiv preprint (continuous-time causal-discovery theory; November 16, 2026)
